scope_note: Primary research supports every affirmative row. Opened body is reference_section; opened abstract is publisher_abstract; indexed primary content remains stored_search_excerpt even if a long excerpt was returned. Failed opens are not recorded as full text. Molecular species, product variants and applications are not separate effects.
comparison_note: Current canonical keys and relevant full principles/conditions compared, including all prior biology batches. Physics12 and information13 reviewed directly; physics13 candidate list received from its author. No semantic overlap found with these pending batches. Generic parents are retained only where the new row describes a substantial intermediate, reaction-center or energy-coupling distinction.

evidence.title: Structural Basis for the Mechanism of ATP-Dependent Acetone Carboxylation
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: activate both acetone and bicarbonate with a single ATP
evidence.finding: Opened introduction, structure results and proposed cycle: nucleotide-bound conformations connect separate phosphorylation and Mn reaction sites. Prior biochemistry plus these structures support activation of both carbon substrates before C–C ligation.
evidence.limits: Phosphoenolacetone/carboxyphosphate trafficking and the detailed Mn-site sequence are a structural rationale, not direct capture of every intermediate. ATP stoichiometry varies among enzymes. Acetophenone and acetone variants are grouped.
evidence.boundary: Biotin carrier carboxylation transfers activated carbon on a covalent cofactor; here both carbon substrates are phosphorylated and brought to the metal site. Internal channeling is an enabling transport step, not the distinguishing chemical transformation. PEP carboxylation is deliberately not a second card in this batch.

evidence.title: Structure of a nascent membrane protein as it folds on the BAM complex
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: release by stepwise exchange of hydrogen bonds
evidence.finding: Opened abstract and public figure captions describe a trapped catalyst–substrate asymmetric hybrid barrel and substrate-assisted release by hydrogen-bond exchange.
evidence.limits: The reported substrate is BamA folding on BamA. The paywalled body was not retrieved. Detailed ordering is not asserted for every outer-membrane substrate or organelle assembly machine.
evidence.boundary: A temporary intermolecular beta-sheet is formed and resolved during membrane folding. This differs from antiaggregation chaperones, capped cages, stable domain-swapped oligomers and Sec lateral partitioning of hydrophobic segments.

evidence.title: Structural insights into the catalytic mechanism of human squalene synthase
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: using presqualene diphosphate (PSPP) as an intermediate
evidence.finding: Opened primary abstract reports two-step reductive head-to-head coupling and structures with substrate analogues and intermediates. Public publisher figure 1 identifies the cyclopropyl intermediate and bond rearrangements.
evidence.limits: NADPH binding is a model supported by mutagenesis, not a fully captured catalytic trajectory. Product reduction variants and different terpene substrates are not separately counted.

supplementary.finding: Indexed publisher figure caption specifies PSPP linkage cleavage and alternative squalene/dehydrosqualene outcomes under different cofactor conditions.

supplementary.title: Mechanism of action and inhibition of dehydrosqualene synthase
supplementary.finding: Indexed primary structural study describes the shared cyclopropyl intermediate pathway; treated as the same family, not an additional effect.

evidence.boundary: Two substrate chains join through a cyclopropylcarbinyl intermediate which then rearranges. Existing polyene cyclization folds one chain into rings, while carbene/SAM cyclopropanation transfers a one-carbon group without this head-to-head reorganization.

evidence.title: Oxidative cleavage of polysaccharides by monocopper enzymes depends on H2O2
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: the reductant is consumed in priming
evidence.finding: Opened abstract reports enzyme assays, oxygen-label experiments and mass spectrometry supporting peroxide-driven oxidative polysaccharide cleavage, including turnover without molecular oxygen.
evidence.limits: The detailed oxygen intermediate is not fully established by this abstract. No universal two-electron/O2 requirement is asserted. C1/C4 positions and cellulose/chitin variants are one effect.

supplementary.title: The molecular basis of polysaccharide cleavage by lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases
supplementary.finding: Indexed primary structures/spectroscopy connect substrate binding geometry with copper-mediated oxidation adjacent to the glycosidic linkage. Author-manuscript PDF open failed, so this remains indexed scope.

evidence.boundary: Copper-driven carbon oxidation destabilizes the glycosidic linkage. This is distinct from hydrolytic anomeric substitution, transient NAD oxidation/elimination/reduction and heme oxygen insertion without glycoside cleavage.

evidence.title: Structure and mechanism of Mycobacterium smegmatis polynucleotide phosphorylase
evidence.finding: Opened primary body reports cryo-EM structures, catalytic-site mutagenesis and the reversible NDP/Pi reaction. Phosphate attacks terminal phosphodiester phosphorus rather than hydrolytic cleavage with water.
evidence.limits: Authors favor a two-metal mechanism but do not exclude alternating single-metal occupancy; their structure does not directly capture every substrate-bound catalytic state. No organism-engineering claim is made.
evidence.boundary: Existing exonuclease describes sequential end removal and polyadenylation uses ATP with pyrophosphate release. Here Pi/NDP exchange conserves a diphosphate product. Glycosidic phosphorolysis attacks anomeric carbon rather than phosphorus.

evidence.title: Redox potential changes during ATP-dependent corrinoid reduction determined by redox titrations with europium(II)–DTPA
evidence.finding: Indexed primary content reports an apparent corrinoid Co(II)/Co(I) potential shift from about −530 to −250 mV with ATP-dependent activation, allowing reduction by a milder donor.
evidence.limits: PMC open returned a challenge and Wiley returned 403. Indexed content was read; no full-text retrieval claimed. ATP binding, hydrolysis and conformational contributions are not generalized to all ATP-dependent electron-transfer families, some of which alter donor potentials or complex dissociation.
evidence.boundary: ATP investment changes the electron-accepting thermodynamics. Generic enzyme electron transfer does not specify uphill energy coupling; flavin bifurcation couples two redox branches. Corrinoid methyl transfer and the ketyl dehydration reaction are downstream chemistry, not this activation route.

evidence.title: Fine-tuning of a radical-based reaction by radical S-adenosyl-L-methionine tryptophan lyase
evidence.finding: Opened abstract reports EPR and isotope-resolved radical intermediates supporting cleavage of the Cα–carboxyl-carbon bond and carboxyl migration, revising the earlier Cα–Cβ fragmentation scheme.
evidence.limits: Specific active-site confinement is essential; not arbitrary solution migration. Later studies refine stepwise radical confinement and cyanide release. The old Cα–Cβ hypothesis is not used as the productive mechanism.

supplementary.title: Crystal Structure of Tryptophan Lyase (NosL): Evidence for Radical Formation at the Amino Group of Tryptophan
supplementary.finding: Primary structure supports amino-nitrogen radical initiation. Its downstream Cα–Cβ proposal is superseded by the 2016 evidence and is not retained.

supplementary.title: Radical S-Adenosyl-l-methionine Tryptophan Lyase (NosL): How the Protein Controls the Carboxyl Radical •CO2− Migration
supplementary.finding: Indexed primary abstract reports crystallography, EPR and quantum/QM-MM analysis of confined carboxyl-radical migration. Detailed elementary steps remain model-dependent.

evidence.boundary: The carboxyl fragment is retained and reattached within the original substrate rather than released as CO2 or converted into iron ligands. CofH/CofG adds an amino-acid fragment to a different substrate before ring closure, a different bond-construction path.

evidence.title: The three-spin intermediate at the O-O cleavage and proton-pumping junction in heme-Cu oxidases
evidence.finding: Opened 2021 Science abstract and public figure captions report magnetic circular dichroism evidence for coupled ferryl, copper(II) and tyrosyl spins in the PM O–O-cleavage intermediate.
evidence.limits: The PMC deposit is dated later than the 2021 publication. Proton-pump topology and the electron donor sequence for every initial redox state are not asserted. This card covers coupled O2 bond cleavage, not a new generic pump application.

supplementary.title: The proton donor for O-O bond scission by cytochrome c oxidase
supplementary.finding: Indexed primary abstract reports time-resolved optical, FTIR and electrometric evidence supporting proton donation from the cross-linked tyrosine during O–O cleavage.

evidence.boundary: The metal pair and covalent organic cofactor collect reducing equivalents for O2 cleavage. P450 oxygen insertion and catalase peroxide disproportionation have different substrate fates and redox cycles. Generic PCET is a parent, not an assertion that this multicomponent cycle is a single elementary concerted step.

evidence.title: Oxidation state of the active-site cysteine in protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: The sulphenyl-amide is a protective intermediate
evidence.finding: Opened primary abstract describes oxidized active-site structures including the cyclic sulphenyl-amide, conformational regulation and protection from irreversible overoxidation.
evidence.limits: A suitable backbone geometry is required. The card does not generalize formation to every sulfenic acid or claim repair after irreversible higher oxidation states.

supplementary.title: Redox regulation of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B involves a sulphenyl-amide intermediate
supplementary.finding: Independent primary abstract identifies the bond between catalytic cysteine sulfur and adjacent main-chain nitrogen and thiol-reversible structural change.

evidence.boundary: The protective trap is an intramolecular S–N cycle, unlike disulfide exchange. Sulfiredoxin repairs the higher sulfinate state through ATP activation and thiosulfinate formation; this is a different intermediate and entry condition.

evidence.title: The identification of carbon dioxide mediated protein post-translational modifications
evidence.finding: Opened body uses carbamate trapping, isotope-sensitive NMR and mass spectrometry to identify reversible CO2 additions to amines in model substrates and proteins.
evidence.limits: Chemical trapping stabilizes a normally reversible adduct; functional regulation is not presumed for every detected site. This card includes general amine capture and does not split proteins from sorbent materials.
evidence.boundary: Neutral amine nitrogen adds to CO2 and changes charge/coordination. Rubisco forms carbon–carbon bonds in its substrate; mineral carbonation makes inorganic salts; urethane formation adds alcohol to isocyanate. Protein carbamylation by cyanate is not conflated with reversible CO2 carbamate.

evidence.title: Transnitrosation between nitrosothiols and thiols
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: attack by the thiolate anion at the nitroso nitrogen atom
evidence.finding: Opened primary abstract reports pH-dependent kinetics consistent with direct thiolate attack at nitroso nitrogen, transferring the nitroso group between thiols.
evidence.limits: Solution-model kinetics support the pathway; no universal intracellular rate or physiological effect is claimed. Free-NO release is not required by this transfer mechanism.
evidence.boundary: The electrophilic center and transferred group are nitroso nitrogen, rather than the sulfur attacked during disulfide exchange. Existing NO signaling describes heme binding. Nucleophilic substitution is a broad parent; this is the weakest parent-boundary row and should be merged into that parent if atom-specific group-transfer pathways are excluded by the final editorial criterion.

evidence.title: Unimolecular net heterolysis of symmetric and homopolar σ-bonds
evidence.finding: Opened abstract and main mechanism discussion describe thermal homolysis followed by selective radical photoexcitation and electron transfer, producing ionic products from symmetric or homopolar bonds.
evidence.limits: Experimental examples are Se–Se and C–Se bonds. Excitation of only one incipient radical is presented as probable symmetry breaking, not a universally directly observed elementary event. This is not a claim that all unpolarized sigma bonds heterolyze under light.
evidence.boundary: Existing radical-generation cards stop at radicals and solvent-cage recombination returns the initial bond. Here a second excitation changes the radical-pair charge state to an ion pair, enabling net heterolysis. It is not SRN1 propagation by electron transfer to the next substrate.

excluded_candidates.reason: Different activation input but shares the carboxyphosphate/enolate terminal chemistry with the accepted double-activation pathway. Not separately counted in this batch; avoid inflation by prephosphorylated substrate variants.

The reconstituted membrane result is real, but the proposed card could be read as recognition plus size-dependent steric exclusion. Excluded conservatively under the strict combination-versus-distinct-path criterion; no assertion that T-cell signaling is fully explained by this partitioning.
excluded_candidates.primary_title: In vitro reconstitution of T cell receptor-mediated segregation of the CD45 phosphatase
excluded_candidates.retrieved_excerpt: absence of any active cellular organization

excluded_candidates.reason: Detailed azacyclopropylcarbinyl intermediate is model-dependent and overlaps the existing PLP radical amino migration and radical-rearrangement families. A distinct final ring size alone is insufficient for this batch.

Not split from the energy-coupled electron-transfer family in the accepted corrinoid activation row. Aromatic reduction product alone also risks duplicating Birch-type reduction. Donor-potential and acceptor-potential variants are explicitly not multiplied.
Existing oxidative-amino-acid-deamination already describes imine formation and hydrolytic deamination. Cofactor identity and substrate class are insufficient here for an additional card.
Thermal movement plus occupancy preventing reverse movement shares the existing polymerization Brownian-ratchet rectification principle. A different blocking protein was not accepted as a new effect.
Existing sulfatase-sulfate-ester-hydrolysis already names the formylglycine hydrate reaction center. No new independent row.
Radical beta cleavage and photodimer restoration risk an application-specific split from existing radical scission and dimer-repair mechanisms. Not added solely for enzyme/substrate identity.

editorial_attention: 12 retained instead of forcing the requested 15–20 through weak mechanistic variants.
Transnitrosation is the closest broad-parent boundary; source and atom-level chemistry are firm, final counting depends on the chosen breadth of nucleophilic-substitution.
Heme–Cu–Tyr row describes O2 cleavage chemistry, not an extra proton-pump card; all detailed pump and universal initial-state claims are excluded.
ATP-dependent corrinoid source is honestly stored_search_excerpt after blocked page opens.
